stated: Reform UK will launch a special division of the Family Court for maintenance and defaults, mandate 50/50 shared parental care where appropriate, and ensure rights of access for grandparents.

source.quote: Reform the Child Maintenance Service We will launch a special division of the Family Court for maintenance and defaults. Share parental care 50/50 where appropriate. Rights of access for grandparents.

bearing_set.reason: Creating a dedicated Family Court division for maintenance and defaults directly addresses justice-system capacity and enforcement effectiveness — a core O5 indicator ('does justice work?').

Mandating 50/50 shared parental care and legislating grandparent access rights constitute new legal entitlements within the family-law rights framework, squarely within O9's scope of civil/legal rights.
Child maintenance enforcement reform directly affects real disposable income for single-parent (typically receiving) households, where unpaid maintenance is a material shortfall in the family budget.

Mandating a 50/50 shared-care default, even with an 'where appropriate' qualifier, is a state-imposed presumption over private family arrangements, constraining parental autonomy — a concrete mechanism affecting freedom from state coercion in intimate decisions.

membership_note: Three genuine bearings: O5 for the court-efficiency and enforcement mechanism; O9 for the equal-treatment/due-process framing around parental and grandparent rights; O10 because a legislated custody presumption — however qualified — places a state mandate over a domain of personal and family autonomy.
